# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 40 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 40 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_040_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Part 2 — On Repentance and Double-Mindedness

**40:1** "Lord," I said, "I wish to ask you one further matter." "Speak," he said. "Lord," I said, "I have heard from certain teachers that there is no other repentance beyond the one we received when we descended into the water and obtained forgiveness of the sins we had previously committed."

**40:2** He said to me: "You have heard correctly, for so it stands. For one who has received forgiveness of sins ought never again to sin, but to abide in purity. Yet since you inquire precisely into all things, I will explain this as well — so as to give no excuse to those who will believe, or to those who have already believed, in the Lord. For those who have already believed or shall believe hereafter have no further repentance of sins, but they do have forgiveness of the sins they previously committed."

**40:3** "For those who were called before these days, the Lord appointed repentance. For the Lord, who searches the heart and foreknows all things, knew the weakness of human beings and the many devices of the devil, that he would work harm against the servants of God and do wickedness against them. Therefore, being compassionate, the Lord had mercy on his creation and established this repentance, and authority over this repentance was given to me."

**40:4** "But I tell you," he said, "if after that great and solemn calling anyone is tempted by the devil and sins, he has one repentance. But if he sins and repents repeatedly, it profits such a man nothing — for with difficulty shall he live."

**40:5** I said to him: "I have been given new life upon hearing these things from you with such precision. For I know that if I add no more to my sins, I shall be saved." "You shall be saved," he said, "you and all who do these things."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and doctrinal precision.*
